title: Build-a-Bot: Teaching Conversational AI Using a Transformer-Based Intent Recognition and Question Answering Architecture
venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the need for more adaptable and flexible AI education tools that let students learn AI by building systems, rather than only learning terminology, use cases, or ethics. The authors argue that existing AI education resources often treat AI systems as black boxes or focus on rule-based chatbot activities, leaving a gap for tools that teach the supervised learning process in an intuitive way.

To address this, the paper proposes Build-a-Bot, an open-source tool that lets students and teachers create customizable conversational AI systems from their own curricular materials. The pipeline includes student data collection and labeling, data augmentation via backtranslation, keyword-based policy filtering, BERT-based intent recognition, and question answering with DistilBERT or T5. The design is presented as a middle-school-appropriate, no-code interface intended for classroom use, with instructors defining intents and contexts and students interacting with each step of the pipeline.

The paper is framed around K-12 AI literacy, especially elementary and middle school contexts, and it draws on constructivist and active learning principles. It includes a sample fifth-grade science testing suite and a machine learning concept suite, but it does not report an actual classroom trial or comparative outcome study. The main conclusion is that Build-a-Bot may help educators of varying technical backgrounds support AI literacy by enabling students to tinker with and understand conversational AI systems, though the authors note that classroom piloting and efficacy testing remain future work.

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: A general conversational AI/chatbot pipeline that uses transformer-based intent recognition and question answering to generate responses to user questions.
identified_tools.use_case: Proposed and prototyped as Build-a-Bot, an open-source classroom tool for students to create custom chatbots from their own course materials and learn AI concepts through the model-building process.

quality_tier_rationale: This is a proposal/prototype paper describing Build-a-Bot and its architecture, not an empirical evaluation of student outcomes. The paper explicitly notes that further work is needed to provide the tool to schools and seek student and teacher evaluations.
impact_tier_rationale: No outcome data are reported, so there is no measurable demonstrated impact on student learning or instructional efficiency. The paper does suggest potential classroom utility, but that remains untested in the text provided.
